chunks: And everything in this book that is narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm has been transmitted by me from Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm.

key_terms.الْحَسَنِ بْنِ الْجَهْمِ: Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, a prominent narrator in Shia hadith literature
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a honorific used for the narrator
key_terms.عَن أَبِيهِ: From his father, indicating a direct paternal link in the chain
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ مَاجِيلَوَيْهَ: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh, a key scholar and narrator

ai.seo_question: Who is the direct transmitter of Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm's narrations in this book?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq provides a specific biographical verification for the narrator Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, a key figure in the Kufan scholarly tradition, by citing his direct teacher, Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh. This explicit chain of transmission underscores the reliability of the hadiths attributed to Al-Hasan ibn Al-Jahm, addressing potential scholarly debates regarding his status as a trustworthy transmitter (thiqa) within the Ja'fari school.
